faq.a: Richmond's north riverfront gateway around Bridgeport Station — planned by the City as Bridgeport Village in the City Centre Area Plan, and in character a heavily industrial and commercial area in transition, with the River Rock Casino Resort at the station and homes concentrated on the Bridgeport Road corridor to the south.

It is the Canada Line junction station: the Richmond–Brighouse branch, the YVR–Airport branch and the Vancouver leg to Waterfront all meet there, and it is also a regional bus exchange with routes including the 403, the 430 Express to Metrotown and the 601 to South Delta and Tsawwassen.

faq.q: Can homes be built in Bridgeport Village?
faq.a: In the village's Urban Centre T5 and General Urban T4 designations the plan states residential use is prohibited; the homes the City documents are on the Bridgeport Road corridor south of the village, including a townhouse rezoning at Bridgeport Road and Shell Road.

faq.q: Do airport rules apply in Bridgeport?
faq.a: Yes — the plan map states the City's Aircraft Noise Sensitive Development Policy applies throughout Bridgeport Village, a City data sheet places sites in Aircraft Noise Sensitive Use Areas 1B and 2, and Federal Airport Zoning Regulation heights govern over the Transit-Oriented Area heights at the station.

faq.q: What flood rules apply in Bridgeport?
faq.a: City data sheets place village sites in Flood Construction Level Area A under the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204, and city-wide Richmond sits in the Fraser River floodplain behind 49 km of dikes and 39 pump stations, designed for a 1:500 flood event with dike raising from 3.5 m to 4.7 m under way.
